scope: Direct deductive verification of the actual three management authorization predicates after TypeScript erasure. Caller hashes identify reviewed integration; they are not caller correctness proofs.
assumptions: Claims and client snapshots are owned native data-property records. Actual callers derive them from browser observations; peer payload claims never establish identity.
JavaScript fresh object identity, TypeScript erasure, parser/extractor, Gillian semantics, verifier and solver are trusted.
Browser event/client/port authenticity, fixed trusted bridge bytes, physical client URL integrity, async rechecks and storage transaction semantics require separate caller/platform contracts.
